scope: Shared DDL admission, persistent/local routing, temporary-table policy and observation visits; existing-owner maintenance, no complete package acceptance.
repairs: Shared DDL visits now require DROP for TRUNCATE, ordered source ALTER/DROP and destination CREATE/INSERT for both rename spellings, ALTER/DROP for sequences and database-scoped ALTER admission.
CREATE LIKE checks source SELECT with Go CREATE denial text; CREATE/ALTER foreign keys check REFERENCES in source order, retaining Go authErr independently of the checked privilege.
Partition DROP/TRUNCATE require DROP; EXCHANGE checks all eight ordered source/destination privileges. Grouped ALTER fails before schema mutation and denied DDL preserves the open transaction.

Go temporary-table admission policy adapts privileges at execution without dropping raw observation visits: local CREATE checks database CREATE TEMPORARY TABLES, queries/DML and local TRUNCATE are exempt where execution resolves the session overlay, DROP SEQUENCE/VIEW keep normal checks.

Persistent sequence/partition exceptions are removed; supported partition operations survive cluster schema refresh, sequence creation refuses a missing durable owner, and local TRUNCATE uses its session owner with Go implicit-commit behavior.
FK default schemas follow the child table; temporary LIKE sources are refused before privilege checks and Go case folding selects local temporary targets.
Existing local, prepared and cluster admission callers reuse the same collector; completed LIKE, RENAME and TRUNCATE summaries retain real source/destination tables.
removals: Single CREATE/ALTER privilege shortcuts replaced by typed action/source visits
Stale sequence/partition session-local routing exceptions and their misleading comments
Repeated cluster/local DDL parsing; original parsed statement is shared with execution

wire_regressions.details: Initial wire exposed missing cluster ALTER-FK admission and unsupported cluster sequence lifecycle. Follow-up reproduced local-temporary TRUNCATE lookup failure, partition ADD metadata loss after schema refresh, and false sequence CREATE success. The unsafe routing exceptions are removed; sequence and ALTER-FK durable owners remain unsupported. The first run included three unsupported positive expectations; only its missing admission is counted as a repaired wire regression. Shadow-source CREATE LIKE supplied one further real failure.

rust_tests.intermediate_failure: Wrong expectation: Go rejects CREATE LIKE from local temporary sources; corrected test only.

resource_recovery.resolution: Recorded and removed the incomplete owned link output and an inactive older smoke executable; preserved compiler/dependency caches; the full locked package build then passed.
